symptoms: Dark brown circular spots with concentric rings on lower/older leaves
Yellowing of tissue surrounding the spots
Leaves eventually wither and drop
causes: Warm, humid conditions with prolonged leaf wetness
Overhead irrigation and poor air circulation
prevention: Rotate crops away from tomato/potato family for 2-3 years
Space plants to improve airflow
Avoid overhead watering; water at the base
Remove and destroy infected plant debris
organic_treatment: Remove and dispose of infected lower leaves promptly
Apply copper-based or biological fungicides labeled for early blight
Mulch to reduce soil splash onto leaves
chemical_treatment: Use a fungicide labeled for early blight on tomato, following local label directions and pre-harvest intervals

symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked lesions on leaves that turn dark brown/black
White fuzzy fungal growth on the underside of leaves in humid weather
Rapid collapse of foliage; dark lesions on stems and fruit
prevention: Plant resistant or tolerant varieties where available
Avoid overhead irrigation
Ensure good airflow and avoid overcrowding
Monitor local blight forecasts during high-risk weather
organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately to slow spread
Apply copper-based fungicides preventively before infection sets in
chemical_treatment: Use a fungicide labeled for late blight on tomato; because it spreads fast, preventive application before disease onset is more effective than curative use

symptoms: No visible disease symptoms; uniform green foliage
prevention: Continue routine monitoring
Maintain balanced watering and fertilization

symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric ring pattern on older leaves
Yellow halo around lesions
Premature leaf drop reducing tuber yield
causes: Plant stress, warm temperatures, and leaf wetness
prevention: Rotate crops with non-solanaceous plants
Maintain adequate plant nutrition to reduce stress
Avoid overhead irrigation
chemical_treatment: Use a fungicide labeled for early blight on potato according to local guidance

White mold growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions
Rapid plant collapse; tuber rot
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed potatoes
Plant resistant varieties where available
Destroy volunteer potato plants and cull piles
organic_treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants promptly
chemical_treatment: Apply a fungicide labeled for late blight on potato before disease pressure builds, per local label directions

prevention: Continue routine monitoring and balanced fertilization

Spots may merge and cause leaf yellowing and drop
Raised, scabby lesions on fruit
causes: Spread by splashing water, rain, and contaminated tools/seed
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants
Avoid working in fields when foliage is wet
Rotate crops and sanitize tools
organic_treatment: Apply copper-based bactericides as a preventive measure
Remove and destroy heavily infected plants
chemical_treatment: Copper-based products remain the primary chemical control; consult local agricultural extension for resistance management

prevention: Continue routine monitoring

symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface
Small black dots within the spots
Orange, tube-like structures on leaf undersides later in season
causes: Fungal pathogen requiring both apple/crabapple and juniper/cedar hosts to complete its life cycle
prevention: Remove nearby juniper/cedar hosts where feasible
Plant resistant apple varieties
Ensure good air circulation
organic_treatment: Apply sulfur-based fungicides preventively in early season
chemical_treatment: Apply a fungicide labeled for cedar apple rust starting at bud break, per local label guidance

symptoms: Small, circular to elongate, reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules rupture and release rust-colored spores
prevention: Plant resistant hybrids where available
Monitor fields during cool, humid periods
organic_treatment: Generally minor impact; cultural controls and resistant varieties are the primary organic strategy
chemical_treatment: Foliar fungicide application may be warranted for severe infections on susceptible hybrids, per local guidance
